::: {.why}
The replication is one of the few exact and non-obvious results in derivatives, it explains what VIX is, and it is a standard interview question because the derivation is short.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the static replication of a variance swap as a weighted portfolio of options and give the weighting.
- Say what the replication assumes and which assumption fails in practice.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Follow the derivation in the Gatheral first Imperial lecture: applying Itô to the log of the price produces realized variance plus a term in the log contract, and the log contract is replicated by a strip of options weighted by the reciprocal of the strike squared. Write it out; it is about half a page.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Implement the replication on your own chain and compare its cost against the fair variance strike implied by VIX-style calculation. The gap is the discretisation error from having finitely many listed strikes, and it is largest exactly when the tails matter, which is the assumption that fails.
:::
:::

## Resources

- [Gatheral — The Volatility Surface, Statics and Dynamics (Imperial lecture 1)](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/media/imperial-college/research-centres-and-groups/cfm-imperial-institute-of-quantitative-finance/events/distinguished-lectures/Gatheral-1st-Lecture.pdf) [reference]{.res-kind}
- [Gatheral — The Volatility Surface (Wiley)](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/The+Volatility+Surface:+A+Practitioner's+Guide-p-9780471792512) [textbook]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
The variance swap replication derived and implemented on a real chain, with the discretisation error against the theoretical strike reported.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Give the option weighting that replicates a variance swap, and say what breaks the replication in practice.
:::
